Both units are members of the Ethiopian federation created out of the SNNPR on 19 August 2023, and the dataset's category word `district` is simply wrong for a first-level federal unit. The ISO 3166-2 register is silent on them - checked 2026-09-18 through pycountry, which lists thirteen ET codes and neither ET-CE nor ET-SE, both codes being this project's own provisional inventions - but the register types every other member `Regional state`, including ET-SW Southwest Ethiopia Peoples, the unit carved out of the same SNNPR in 2021, which is the closest published analogue. Wikidata's P31 for Q122415622 and Q122148951 is `region of Ethiopia` (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q122415622, https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q122148951), the same generic gloss it gives ET-SW, so P31 draws no distinction either way and loses to the specific term under the ruling that prefers the established English word over a catch-all. English Wikipedia is unambiguous: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_Ethiopia says `There are twelve regional states and two chartered cities`, and the stored articles (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Ethiopia_Regional_State rev 1372646837, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Ethiopia_Regional_State rev 1367343950) set `type = Regional state` in the infobox and open `is a regional state in Ethiopia`. Independently, the units' own governments use the term in English on their .gov.et sites - the South Ethiopia Regional State Office of the President, https://www.southethiopiarspo.gov.et/overview/ - and it is part of each unit's own official English name, which is also this project's `placeEng`. Consulted and set aside: the 1995 FDRE Constitution's Article 47 (https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Ethiopia_1994), whose English says `Member States ... The State of Tigray` and so predates and does not name either unit.

The local term is kilil (pl. kililoch), which English does not use as a type word - it appears only glossed: Britannica https://www.britannica.com/place/Ethiopia/Constitutional-framework writes `ethnically based kililoch (regional states; singular kilil)`, and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subdivisions_of_Ethiopia gives `regions (kililoch), or alternatively regional state`. So the choice is between two English words, and `regional state` is the specific one actually in use - it is the ISO 3166-2 register's own category for ET, and the states' own official English names carry it (`Amhara National Regional State`). Wikidata's P31 type word is the generic `region`; the ruling's preference for the specific form over the catch-all OVERRIDES Wikidata here.
